title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: how many transport documents a customer may hold
content:
## Scope

This clause of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents policy governs how many transport documents one customer may hold at the same time. It applies whenever a draft transport document is created for a customer.

## Formal clause

1. A customer may hold any number of transport documents at once. There is no cap per customer: the company sets no maximum number of documents for one documentation party.
2. Each transport document covers exactly one booking.
3. How documents combine on one and the same booking is governed by the company's one-document-in-force-per-booking rule, not by this clause.

## Restated as condition and result

| Question asked of the record | Answer under this clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a ceiling on documents per customer? | No, there is no cap per customer. |
| Can one document cover two bookings? | No, each document covers exactly one booking. |
| Does this clause decide whether a second document may exist on the same booking? | No, that is decided by the one-document-in-force-per-booking rule. |

## Points of judgement

- **Hypothetical case:** a freight forwarder already holds documents on several of its bookings and submits shipping instructions for a further booking. The number of documents it already holds is not, under this clause, a ground to refuse the new draft.
- The count of documents a customer holds is never compared against any limit, because no limit exists for this product.
